relationships.subject: nitroglycerin
relationships.evidence_quote: NTG was administered intraperitoneally, resulting in migraine-like pain and associated behaviors that were measured in animals using two independent behavioral metrics—facial grimace and light avoidance/movement.

relationships.subject: CGRP receptor
relationships.evidence_quote: NTG thus induced CLR/RAMP1–dependent migraine-like responses.

relationships.subject: CGRP
relationships.evidence_quote: In cultured human lymphatic endothelial cells, CGRP was found to induce formation of continuous, nonpermeable VE-cadherin junctions, involving activation of ERK-CREB phosphorylation.

relationships.subject: CGRP
relationships.evidence_quote: CGRP signaling was thus demonstrated to be required for VE-cadherin linear junction formation at MLV endpoints to render MLVs impermeable and to impair their drainage function (1).

relationships.subject: CGRP
relationships.evidence_quote: Cultures of human lymphatic endothelial cells exposed to CGRP peptides confirmed the upregulation of markers of lymphatic vascular-immune interactions, including connexin 47, MAdCAM1, and pentraxin3

key_findings: Commentary on Nelson-Maney et al.: lymphatic CGRP receptor signaling mediates NTG-induced migraine-like pain in mice.
CGRP drives VE-cadherin junction formation and impairs CSF uptake and drainage by meningeal lymphatic vessels.
